questions.q:
Which of the following idiom given in the alternatives has the meaning?
Enjoy oneself very much
options: Have a nick of a time
Have a click of a time
Have a whale of a time
Have a shell of a time
questions.solution:
Having a whale of a time means enjoying oneself very much.

**Answer: Have a whale of a time**

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word from the given options.
questions.solution:
Fascination is the correct spelling. It includes sc after fa.

**Answer: Fascination**

questions.q:
Select the option with the correct spelling that can replace the underlined word in the given sentence. If the spelling in the given sentence is already correct, choose Option "No replacement required".

The doctor diagnosed her with __kleptomenia__, a disorder that caused her to steal compulsively.
questions.solution:
The correct spelling is kleptomania, referring to a compulsive urge to steal.

**Answer: kleptomania**

questions.q:
There are four underlined words in the sentence given below. One of them is misspelt. Choose the option with the misspelt word.

The summit emphasised __multilateral__ __cooperation__ to address __pressing__ global issues such as climate change and __terrorisim__.
questions.solution:
Terrorisim is misspelled. The correct spelling is terrorism.

**Answer: terrorisim**

questions.q: Choose the misspelt word from the given options.
questions.solution:
Ludicurous is incorrect. The correct spelling is ludicrous.

**Answer: Ludicurous**

questions.q: Choose the word that is most opposite in meaning to **“dig”**.
questions.solution:
Dig means remove earth. Fill means put material into a hole and is the contrasting action.

**Answer: Fill**

questions.q: Choose the word that is the antonym of **Get back**.
questions.solution:
Get back means regain or recover. Lose is its opposite.

**Answer: Lose**

questions.q: The word "bank" is a homonym. In which sentence does it mean the side of a river?
options: She deposited her salary in the bank.
They had a picnic on the bank of the Ganga.
He decided to bank on his friends for support.
The central bank controls the country’s money supply.
questions.solution:
Bank means a river’s edge in They had a picnic on the bank of the Ganga.

**Answer: They had a picnic on the bank of the Ganga.**

questions.q:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who has no money.
questions.solution:
A pauper is a very poor person without means. A miser may have money but avoids spending it.

**Answer: Pauper**

questions.q:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An athletic event comprising ten different events.
questions.solution:
A decathlon combines ten athletics events. Pentathlon has five and heptathlon seven.

**Answer: Decathlon**

questions.q:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

People believed that he was innocent.
options: It will believe that he was innocent.
He was believe to be innocent by people.
It was believed that he was innocent.
His innocence was believe by people.
questions.solution:
The impersonal passive uses It was believed that…. This preserves the original past tense.

**Answer: It was believed that he was innocent.**

questions.q:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

Didn't the manager inform all the employees about the new rule?
options: Weren't all the employees informed about the new rule by the manager?
Wasn't all the employees informed about the new rule by the manager?
Didn't all the employees informed about the new rule by the manager?
Doesn't all the employees informed about the new rule by the manager?
questions.solution:
All the employees is plural. A past passive negative question therefore begins Weren’t all the employees informed…?

**Answer: Weren't all the employees informed about the new rule by the manager?**

questions.q:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?

You are requested to come early tomorrow.
options: I request your early coming tomorrow.
questions.solution:
The active polite request is Please come early tomorrow.

**Answer: Please come early tomorrow.**

questions.q:
In the given question, a sentence is divided into four parts and given in the alternatives (A), (B), (C), and (D). There is an error in one part. Choose the alternative containing that part of the sentence that has the error. Choosing the alternative with the error will be the answer.

Johnsy was so angry with the stranger that she threw her sandals to him hurting just above his right eyebrow.
options: stranger that she threw her sandals to him
hurting just above his right eyebrow.
questions.solution:
To throw something intending to hit someone, use at, not to. The third segment is incorrect.

**Answer: stranger that she threw her sandals to him**

questions.q:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

Their surprise gift came ________ the form of a new laptop.
questions.solution:
The fixed expression is in the form of. Therefore in completes the sentence.

**Answer: in**

questions.q:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: “No Improvement Required.”

The prestigious award was given to the scientist for his __groundshaking research in genetics__.
questions.solution:
Groundbreaking means innovative or pioneering. It is the correct word for the scientist’s research.

**Answer: groundbreaking research in genetics**

questions.q:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

The child wanted to hear the story ________ Vikramaditya.
questions.solution:
Use about to identify the subject of a story: the story about Vikramaditya.

**Answer: about**

questions.q:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. At half-past eleven that night he drove up to the entrance of the Paris Hotel
A. He was admitted.
B. Grohol sky was packing his things in a portmanteau, Liza was sitting at the table trying on bracelets.
C. He went noisily upstairs and knocked at the door of Grohol sky's apartments.
D. They were both frightened when Bugrov went in to them.
S2. They fancied that he had come for Liza and had brought back the money which he had taken in haste without reflection.
questions.solution:
He first goes upstairs and knocks (C), then is admitted (A). The scene inside is described (B), followed by their frightened reaction (D).

**Answer: CABD**

questions.q:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."

__The employees, having completing the rigorous training program,__ felt well prepared for the upcoming challenges.
options: The rigorous training program, having been completed by the employees
Having completed the employees rigorous training program,
Having completed the rigorous training program, the employees
questions.solution:
After having, use the past participle completed. The phrase should modify the employees: Having completed the rigorous training program, the employees… .

**Answer: Having completed the rigorous training program, the employees**
